milestone: M49 Headless Mode Pack Update Drive

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets public headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive carry existing post-fetch Mode Pack route targets through durable session authority.
Connects provenance verification, approval, and replacement continuation targets to the public Mode Pack update drive path.
Requires explicit target authorization, persisted route agreement, bounded one-step execution, and matching replay identity before side effects.
Preserves run-session evidence and fails closed when subordinate route evidence is absent or mismatched during replay.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development directly, with supporting progress for mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, and persistent_structured_ledger.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive can carry bounded provenance verification, approval, and replacement Mode Pack targets through public run-control after selected-candidate fetch.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: headless.continue_once can perform these later continuations, but public run-control only exposed registry-selection and selected-candidate fetch targets, leaving scheduled callers to own later route glue.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still stall after fetch or leave durable session authority to complete verification, approval, and replacement.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M49.1 fetched an already-routed selected candidate and M49.2 bootstrapped registry selection into fetch with fetch replay integrity; M49.3 expands later route dispatch.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. Existing headless.run.advance and headless.run.drive are extended with bounded target fields and delegate to existing continuation authority.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. It reuses bounded run-control and continuation evidence rather than adding reports, histories, digests, verdicts, inspections, or readiness summaries.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates explicit later Mode Pack run-control targets, forwards them through typed continuation authority, preserves session checkpoints, and fails closed when subordinate routed evidence is missing or mismatched.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Scheduled callers can keep the Mode Pack update route chain inside durable Rust-owned run-control beyond selected-candidate fetch.
answers.milestone_progress: M49 moves from bootstrap/fetch reachability toward public drive coverage of the existing post-fetch Mode Pack update route boundaries.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M49.3 updates the current and archived value manifests for the closed typed Mode Pack route dispatcher expansion.

exit_criteria: headless.run.advance can carry bounded provenance verification, approval, and replacement targets from matching persisted route boundaries
headless.run.drive can pass the same bounded targets through its first runtime-owned advance
routed later Mode Pack replay fails closed when subordinate checkpoint evidence is missing or mismatched
runtime rejects stale progress, wrong route, mixed target, missing target, and invalid budget before side effects
VSIX protocol validators accept the bounded later Mode Pack run-control targets and reject raw/unknown fields
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior tests cover public headless.run.advance dispatch for provenance verification and approval after selected-candidate fetch
Rust behavior tests cover public headless.run.drive first-advance dispatch for selected approved candidate replacement
Rust replay tests cover missing and mismatched later Mode Pack targets before returning replayed run-control evidence
VSIX protocol tests validate run-control params with later typed targets and raw field rejection
